story:
Marquis Almen is the largest peer on the Roll and the court's only prophet, and the court has never once believed him. He belongs to High Lord Saeor's household at the far east end of the hollow, and he is so big that he stands outside his lord's hall because he does not fit easily in it. In the Uncounted Age he told the lords of the east what was going to happen to them, accurately, and they ignored him, and it happened. At the Feast of Thrones he told High Lord Saeor that the hungry one would eat nineteen and the rest would kneel, before the first lord was eaten. Saeor did not believe him then either, and knelt.

Almen sees the shapes of things before they come. He does not see them clearly. He said, in the Fourth Roll, that the roof of the hollow would open in three places and that the light coming down would be the colour of the frontier; nobody knew what a frontier was. The court remembered it when the doors opened in the age of the realm wars, and still did not believe him about anything else. He says now that the Master will one day be fought by mortals who do not come down a door. Nobody knows what that means either.

The princes do one thing with him. When they keep their wagers on which realm will hold the frontier next, they send to Almen to ask, and then bet against what he tells them, since he is never believed and they assume he must be wrong. They lose. The Chancellor records the wagers at his table and has noted that the princes have lost every wager Almen was consulted on. Almen stands outside Saeor's hall with Duke Zepor and Earl Oraxus, and since the doors opened he has told the mortals who reach him how many of them will go back up the eastern stair. The first he told, a Hibernian company out of Tir na Nog in the first winter, did not believe him, and the bards who came home said afterwards that they should have.
legend: Almen is huge and stands just outside High Lord Saeor's hall at the far east, with Duke Zepor and Earl Oraxus. Level 70, no script. His size makes him easy to target and hard to see past, so watch the pull and do not let him body-block your view of Saeor's room. Kill Zepor, Oraxus and Almen before Saeor, who heals by a whole player's health every time he kills one. Players say he tells each raid how many will come back, and Hibernian raids, who meet him early from the eastern stair, have started keeping count of whether he is right. He is, they say, more often than they would like.

loremasterTopic.text: The prophet of High Lord [Saeor]'s household, too big for his lord's hall, who sees the shape of things before they come and is never believed. He foretold the three doors. The princes bet against him and lose every time. He tells each raid how many will go back up the stair.

bookPage: From a Hibernian captain's tally, notched on a hazel stick and kept at the College of Bards in Tir na Nog: Almen at the east, first night: he said eleven of us would go back up. Eleven did. Second night: he said thirty. Twenty-nine; the bard went back for a dropped harp and came up after, so I am counting him as right. Third night: he said none, and we turned back at the Ward and went up the stair, every one of us, out of spite. I do not know whether that proves him wrong, or whether that was what he meant all along.
